# Resource: stripe_transfer_reversal

A reversal of a transfer, which moves some or all of the transfer's amount back from the connected account to the platform. Without `amount`, it reverses what remains of the transfer. Only `metadata` changes after creation.

~> A transfer reversal can move real money. In a live-mode Stripe account, creating or changing one fails at plan time unless the provider sets `allow_live_money_movement = true`. Reading or importing one never does. The provider asks Stripe for the account's mode. See the Managing Test Data guide.

~> Stripe cannot delete or undo a transfer reversal. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the transfer reversal, fail at plan time. To stop managing a transfer reversal, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_transfer" "payout_share" {
  amount      = 1500
  currency    = "usd"
  destination = "acct_123"
}

# Move part of the transfer back to the platform. Without `amount`, the rest is reversed.
resource "stripe_transfer_reversal" "returned_item" {
  transfer = stripe_transfer.payout_share.id
  amount   = 500
  metadata = { reason = "returned item" }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `transfer` - (Required) The ID of the parent object. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

The following arguments are optional:

* `amount` - (Optional) A positive integer in cents (or local equivalent) representing how much of this transfer to reverse. Can only reverse up to the unreversed amount remaining of the transfer. Partial transfer reversals are only allowed for transfers to Stripe Accounts. Defaults to the entire transfer amount. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string which you can attach to a reversal object. This will be unset if you POST an empty value. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `refund_application_fee` - (Optional) Boolean indicating whether the application fee should be refunded when reversing this transfer. If a full transfer reversal is given, the full application fee will be refunded. Otherwise, the application fee will be refunded with an amount proportional to the amount of the transfer reversed. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `balance_transaction` - Balance transaction that describes the impact on your account balance.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `destination_payment_refund` - Linked payment refund for the transfer reversal.
* `source_refund` - ID of the refund responsible for the transfer reversal.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a transfer reversal whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_transfer_reversal.returned_item

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_transfer_reversal.returned_item
```

The transfer reversal stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a transfer reversal using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_transfer_reversal.returned_item
  id = "tr_123/trr_456"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_transfer_reversal.returned_item
  identity = {
    transfer = "tr_123"
    id       = "trr_456"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `transfer` (String) The ID of the parent transfer.
* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the transfer reversal.

Using `terraform import`, import a transfer reversal using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_transfer_reversal.returned_item tr_123/trr_456
```

-> Stripe does not return `description` or `refund_application_fee`, so an imported reversal has them null.
